Independent vertex-by-vertex union-mask dynamic program on literal hyperedges, retaining minimum cardinality and tied count per state: all 70 cases m=1…14, r∈{3,4,5,7,12} agreed. Replay: python /workspace/checks/hyperpath_cover.py
correctness.rationale: A private vertex covers a length-3 edge interval and a junction a length-4 interval before clipping. The bound q=ceil(m/4) is attained for m≥2 by using junctions 2,6,…,4q−6 and last junction min(4q−2,m−1); the last interval reaches m and starts no later than the first uncovered edge, with q=1 interpreted as just the last junction. An optimum cannot include nested or equal intervals. For increasing ends and starts, the width deficit telescopes to the sum of private bits, consecutive overlaps and the two overhang bits. Since t≤3, an overlap equal to 3 forces length 4 on both sides; all reconstructed endpoint increments are positive. The first start and last end force all reconstructed intervals to be valid: ending at most m+1 implies start at most m−1 for length 3 and m−2 for length 4. Private choices have weight a−1 plus one for each coincident path endpoint. For q≥2 put G=1+az/(1−z); the claimed series is G^(q−2)(G−az³/(1−z))²/(1−z), which through z³ equals G^q/(1−z)−2az³. Its coefficient is sum_k binom(q,k)binom(t,k)a^k minus 2a when t=3. Single-vertex covers at m=1,2,3,4 count r,2r−1,r,1 directly. Zero defect forces exact width-four tiling, hence uniqueness.
residual_risks: Finite replay only corroborates the reasoning. Read the slogan's residue-four phrase as selection of a polynomial; except in the rigid case its value also depends on q, as stated precisely in RESULT.md.
